business_problem: Sanofi wants to reduce the time, cost, and bias involved in drug discovery, where researchers must evaluate vast numbers of compounds and need richer disease, protein, molecule, clinical, and real-world data to support AI-driven research.
solution_summary: Sanofi describes an in-house AI and machine-learning approach for drug R&D that combines broad scientific and clinical data collection with modeling and simulation workflows. The implementation centers on building high-quality, diverse data foundations for disease biology, protein interactions, molecule behavior, and patient outcomes so AI models can be used in discovery. Sanofi says its teams integrate bioinformatics and omics data with inputs from smart devices and wearables used in decentralized clinical trials, then expand internal data libraries with patient data from clinical trials and real-world datasets. Those datasets are used to discover and validate digital biomarkers, study small and large molecules, and support faster candidate selection. Cross-functional research, development, and digital teams operate the workflow, while collaborations with Owkin, Exscientia, Atomwise, and Insilico Medicine extend Sanofi's discovery efforts.
data_flow: Sanofi aggregates disease, protein, molecule, clinical-trial, real-world, bioinformatics, omics, smart-device, and wearable data into growing internal data libraries. AI and machine-learning models run on those curated datasets to identify digital biomarkers, analyze small and large molecules, and accelerate drug-discovery decisions.
integration_points: Wearables used in decentralized clinical trials
business_outcome: Sanofi aims to accelerate pharmaceutical research, better understand biology, identify the right molecules faster, and deliver therapies to patients more quickly by applying AI and machine learning to drug discovery.
architecture_clues: Cross-disciplinary workflow spanning research, development, and digital teams
Growing internal data libraries built from scientific, clinical, and real-world sources
Use of digital biomarkers in disease research
Decentralized clinical trials contribute wearable and smart-device data
External AI-drug-discovery collaborations supplement in-house R&D
